Pennsylvania households should prepare for higher electric bills as generation prices increase across the state beginning June 1, the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission (PUC) announced Wednesday. All regulated utilities will adjust their electric generation rates on the same day, just as summer air-conditioning use typically begins to climb. The changes affect the Price to Compare, which is the rate per kilowatt-hour charged to customers who receive default service from their utility instead of selecting a competitive electric generation supplier. In the Lehigh Valley, Met-Ed is raising its rate by 7.6%, while PPL Electric Utilities is increasing its rate by 1.5%. PECO estimates a price increase of more than 14% for small businesses, while UGI Electric and Penelec customers will see increases exceeding 12% and 6%, respectively. For many residential customers, generation charges represent around 50% or more of a total electric bill.
